notes: §1985:VI.6.19.4 GR1: the selected items of identifier-1 are moved to those of identifier-2 and 'The results are the same as if the user had referred to each pair of corresponding identifiers in separate MOVE statements.' CorrespondingBinder.Bind selects the pairs (CorrMatch) and binds each as an ordinary MOVE through MoveBinder.BindMoveOf, and CorrespondingEmitter.Emit renders them in identifier-1's declaration order through the one MOVE emitter, so each pair converts, edits and aligns as its own MOVE would: that part conforms and is what the witness exercises (alphanumeric and numeric pairs, an unmatched item untouched). No edition arm exists, and the group operands are identified ONCE: CorrAccess anchors a subscripted group in a statement local that CorrespondingEmitter.EmitHoists assigns before the first pair. That is the later rule, §2023:14.9.25.4 GR11's exception ('the subscript value used is that resulting from the evaluation of the subscript at the start of the execution of the statement'), which 1985 does not have: separate MOVE statements each evaluate their own subscripts (§1985:VI.6.19.4 GR2), so a pair that stores into a subscript of the group operand moves the later pairs' element. The rule's change record names this case. With one such subscript the frozen result equals one order of the separate statements; with two it equals none (repro). The selection conditions themselves are the rows of §1985:VI.6.4.3 (kb/Work PB5105 is the level-66 / USAGE INDEX one), not this rule.

next.reason: 1985 GR1: the results are 'the same as if the user had referred to each pair of corresponding identifiers in separate MOVE statements', so each implied MOVE evaluates its own subscripts. §2023:14.9.25.4 GR11 keeps that equivalence 'except that if subscripting is specified for identifier-3 or identifier-4, the subscript value used is that resulting from the evaluation of the subscript at the start of the execution of the statement'. A conforming 1985 program can observe it: MOVE CORR A (I OF B) TO B, where B and the table element A each contain an item I, alters the subscript mid-statement; 1985 re-evaluates it for later pairs, 2023 does not. 1985 GR2's once-only rule is format 1's only. §2023:14.9.25.3 SR13 states the sending/receiving roles of the corresponding items.
